title: Complete profile lifecycle, composition, and upgrades
description:
Complete the profile lifecycle after the adoption-focused v1.0 MVP by adding local packages, deterministic multi-profile composition, variables, durable semantic ownership, drift-aware reconfiguration, and safe upgrades on top of the shared v1.0 repository-materialization foundation.

## Background

The completed v1.0 profiles MVP ships one immutable embedded `jit-dogfood` package, minimal list/show/apply and init integration, dry-run planning, package-level provenance, semantic contribution merging, managed assets and regions, overlay validation, recoverable publication, audit events, JSON output, schema exposure, and adopter documentation. This epic owns only the remaining lifecycle and composition delta; it must extend those contracts rather than reimplement the v1.0 planner, transaction kernel, or projection machinery.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Embedded and explicitly addressed local-directory profiles use one versioned package model, work offline, reject local shadowing of embedded IDs, and support repeatable ordered profile selection for initialization, application, validation, diff, reconfiguration, and upgrade without remote discovery.
- [hard] REQ-02: Profile dependencies, incompatibilities, compatible JIT ranges, and multi-profile contribution graphs resolve deterministically; missing dependencies, cycles, incompatible selections, unsafe paths or symlinks, undeclared executable assets, and conflicting contributions fail before publication.
- [hard] REQ-03: Multi-profile semantic composition deduplicates identical shared contributions, records shared ownership, and rejects differing definitions without an order-based winner, including type-level conflicts and multiple projections targeting the same managed document.
- [hard] REQ-04: Explicitly non-secret profile variables resolve in the order manifest default, values file, manifest-declared environment variable, then repeatable `--set`, and one declared reference/templating model applies them to supported semantic values and generated text so stored resolved values support deterministic reconfiguration; profiles expose no secret-value input, interpolation, persistence, or audit channel.
- [hard] REQ-05: Repository-local applied-profile records migrate the v1.0 minimal provenance format and then record per-profile origin, version, compatibility, resolved non-sensitive inputs, package identity, and per-file or per-semantic-key ownership without becoming an authority for declared repository configuration.
- [hard] REQ-06: `jit profile list`, `show`, `validate`, `diff`, reapply/reconfigure, and `upgrade` cover embedded, applied, and explicitly addressed local packages with stable human output, `--json` envelopes, command/schema exposure, dry-run support for mutations, and audit events that record variable names and source kinds without copying resolved values.
- [hard] REQ-07: Reconfiguration and upgrade use three-way ownership checks: untouched profile-owned content updates, concurrent user/profile changes produce actionable conflicts, shared content retains surviving owners, and only unchanged solely-owned content may be removed as part of an upgrade.
- [hard] REQ-08: Profile lifecycle mutations use the v1.0 shared repository materialization planner and recoverable transaction boundary so complete multi-profile plans, derived repository state, ownership records, and audit events validate and publish atomically, idempotently, and without requiring Git.
- [hard] REQ-09: The embedded `jit-dogfood` package and repositories with v1.0 applied records continue to work without reauthoring package content, duplicating workflow inventories, or weakening config-declared source-of-truth boundaries.
- [hard] REQ-10: Canonical adopter documentation explains local package authoring, composition, variables, ownership, drift, reconfiguration, and upgrades while citing or projecting existing profile, rule, gate, and workflow facts rather than copying them.
- [hard] REQ-11: Automated tests cover local packages, multiple-profile selection and graph resolution, shared and conflicting ownership, non-secret variable precedence, reference rendering, and absence of a secret-input surface, v1.0 record migration, reconfiguration, three-way upgrades, rollback and recovery, Git-free use, audit output, JSON envelopes, schema exposure, and compatibility with the embedded `jit-dogfood` package.
- [hard] REQ-12: Lifecycle capabilities use one canonical package resolver, composition engine, ownership model, and publication path; each cutover removes the superseded path in the same change, and support for v1.0 repositories uses a durable versioned migration into the canonical record rather than adapters, dual formats, fallback behavior, temporary compatibility code, or duplicated workflow inventories.

## Decisions

- D-01: v1.1 extends the adoption-focused v1.0 MVP; it does not replace or fork the v1.0 package, planner, projection, or transaction contracts.
- D-02: Package discovery remains embedded plus explicit local directory. Remote registries and implicit filesystem search are deferred.
- D-03: Multi-profile composition is semantic and conflict-safe: identical contributions share ownership and different definitions fail without selection-order precedence.
- D-04: Applied records are provenance and ownership evidence, never an alternative source of truth for declared repository configuration.
- D-05: Upgrades may remove unchanged solely-owned content as part of replacing an installed version, but a general profile-removal command is deferred beyond v1.1.
- D-06: Profile variables are explicitly non-secret and persistable because deterministic reconfiguration requires their resolved values. Packages may configure an environment-variable name as ordinary text, but profiles never receive the referenced runtime secret.
- D-07: Every lifecycle extension must be the long-term SSOT design. No temporary command, record, package, merge, ownership, or publication path may be introduced to stage later cleanup.

## Risks

- RISK-01: Per-key ownership can become a shadow configuration database; records must describe contribution identity and observed ownership, while final behavior continues to derive from repository registries.
- RISK-02: Three-way upgrades can delete user intent if the base is ambiguous; migration and ownership checks must fail closed when v1.0 evidence is insufficient.
- RISK-03: Users can mistake profile variables for a secret channel; manifests, CLI help, schema, and tests must make the non-secret contract explicit and reject any sensitive-variable declaration or secret indirection surface.
- RISK-04: Composition can duplicate the v1.0 materialization engine; the v1.0 epic is an implementation dependency and its shared primitives are the only publication path.

## Notes

Profile removal, remote package registries or downloads, arbitrary installation hooks, web UI profile management, and language-specific CI profiles are outside this epic. General removal remains deferred beyond v1.1 as confirmed by the owner.
